verdicts.quote_a: 692 public training cases of 867 (Elekta A 120, B 107, C 120, D 120; Varian F 92, G 133); 375,618 projections; 771.1 GB at verification (754 GB by du on 2026-09-25)
verdicts.explanation: The atlas (17 October 2026) and the registry (rendered 2026-10-20) describe the same holding, the 692 public COBRA2026 cases with 375,618 projections, but name three different measurements: 771.1 GB at verification, 754 GB by du on 2026-09-25, and 808.615 GB on Ceph. Neither page states its units: 808.615 GB is 753.1 GiB, which du -h prints as 754G, so the du and Ceph figures may be one size in two units, and what the verification figure summed is not said. The imaging-holding page (8 October 2026) likewise carries both 771 GB for the source and 809 GB for the COBRA2026 folder on Ceph.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry 808.615 GB as the size of the COBRA2026 folder on Ceph (registry), and keep the atlas's 771.1 GB only as the size at verification, each with its basis named; a byte count of the folder beside the verified file list would show whether the three figures are one size in different units.

verdicts.quote_a: the pseudo-label arm that would have used it was measured and refuted (about 19 points of anomalous accuracy)
verdicts.quote_b: none; pseudo-labels cut anomalous accuracy 20 points
verdicts.explanation: The atlas (17 October 2026), on the IEEE DataPort lateral 236 films, says the pseudo-label arm was measured and refuted at about 19 points of anomalous accuracy; the registry (rendered 2026-10-20) says on its NHANES II unannotated record that pseudo-labels cut anomalous accuracy 20 points, and on its lateral 236 record that 'the pseudo-label arm was refuted'. Neither page gives the accuracies behind its figure. Naming Vertebrae Without an Anchor (17 September 2026) does: pseudolabel training lowered anomalous exact naming in the isolated stack on real film from 87.2% to 66.8%, a drop of 20.4 points, which it and Naming Vertebrae Without CT (18 September 2026) call twenty points; no page read here gives a figure that rounds to 19.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry 20 points (registry), with its basis from Naming Vertebrae Without an Anchor: anomalous exact naming on real film 87.2% with bank v2 against 66.8% with the pseudolabelled bank v5; the atlas's 'about 19' should read about 20.
